October 12, 36.

The Commissioner of Police.
Macao.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of your
letter dated September 22, 1936 and in reply to inform
you that Venedict Alexandrovitch Lovtsoff, Russian, was
born on March 4, 1892, at Irkutsk, Siberia. He arrived
in Shanghai in 1928 and two years later registered him-
self as a dental surgeon with the Health Department of
the French Municipal Council. Up to the time of his
departure Lovtsoff continued to practice his profession
in the French Concession.

While in Shanghai Lovtsoff did not come to the
notice of the Police Authorities in connection with
any political or criminal activity.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
（批：21/1 5/11）
F. W. Gerrard
Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of your
letter dated September 22, 1936, and in reply to inform
you that Venedict Alexandrovitch Lovtsoff, Russian, was
born on March 4, 1892, at Irkutsk, Siberia. From early
boyhood to 1923 he resided in Vladivostock. Following
the occupation of this city by the Red Forces, Lovtsoff
continued to reside there but later proceeded to Tomsk
where he graduated from the Tomsk Dental School in 1924.
He then practised as a dental surgeon in Blagoveschensk-
on-Amur where he is also believed to have been officially
engaged by the various Soviet Government establishments.
In 1925 Lovtsoff arrived in Harbin, claiming he had
escaped from Soviet Russia, and it is reported that he
brought with him a large sum of money which he misappro-
priated from certain Soviet Government organs during an
uprising in Blagoveschensk. During 1927 and 1928 Lovtsoff
was employed as a dentist with the Russian Detachments of
the Chinese Army at Tsinanfu, Shantung. He arrived in
Shanghai in 1928 and two years later registered himself
as a dental surgeon with the Health Department of the
French Municipal Council. While in Shanghai he is said
to have lost a considerable amount of money through
gambling. Up to the time of his departure Lovtsoff was
still practising his profession in the French Concession.

While in Shanghai Lovtsoff did not come to the notice
of the Police Authorities in connection with any political
or criminal activity.

在上海期间，Lovtsoff 未因任何政治或犯罪活动引起警方当局的注意。

Made by D.S. Makaroff Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Venedict Alexandrovitch Lovtsoff, Russian, was born on
March 4, 1892 at Irkutsk, Siberia. From his early boyhood to
1923, he resided in Vladivostock, Maritime Province, where he
studied in the 1st Primary School. In 1919 he married Anna
Michailovna nee Novikoff (his present wife) in Vladivostock
and in 1921 a daughter Zoia was born to them.

During the later part of 1922, when Vladivostock was
occupied by the Red forces, Lovtsoff did not migrate from Russia
with the rest of White citizens, but remained there, and soon
afterwards proceeded to Tomsk, where he entered the Tomsk Dental
School, from which he graduated in 1924.

Later he proceeded to Blagoveschensk-on-Amur, and establish-
ed himself as a dental surgeon there.

He is also believed to have been officially engaged by the
various Soviet government establishments at that city.

In 1924 a son Eugene was born to them in Blagoveschensk.
In 1925 Lovtsoff suddenly appeared in Harbin accompanied by his
family and stating that he had escaped from Soviet Russia, duly
registered himself with the local Police authorities as well
as Russian Emigrants' Committee, and was issued with emigrants'
registration papers to that effect.

It is reported that at the time of his arrival in Harbin,
he was in possession of quite a large sum of money which he
misappropriated from certain Soviet governmental institutions
during one of the uprisings in Blagoveschensk. This was also
stated to be the main reason of his flight from the Soviet.

In 1927 Lovtsoff proceeded to Tsinanfu, where he joined
Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army, and served as a dentist amongst
Russian detachments up to 1928.

制作人：警佐 Makaroff 转发人：**〔此处转录不清〕**

俄国人 Venedict Alexandrovitch Lovtsoff 于1892年3月4日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。从幼年至1923年，他居住在滨海省符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），并在第一小学就读。1919年，他在符拉迪沃斯托克与 Anna Michailovna（婚前姓 Novikoff）（即其现任妻子）结婚，1921年生下一女 Zoia。

1922年下半年，当符拉迪沃斯托克被红军占领时，Lovtsoff 并未随其他白俄公民离开俄国，而是留在那里，不久后前往托木斯克，进入托木斯克牙科学校学习，并于1924年毕业。

后来他前往阿穆尔河畔布拉戈维申斯克，并在那里开业成为牙科医师。

据信，他当时也受雇于该市的各种苏联政府机构。

1924年，他们的儿子 Eugene 在布拉戈维申斯克出生。1925年，Lovtsoff 突然携家人出现在哈尔滨，声称已从苏俄逃脱，随即在当地警察当局以及俄国侨民委员会正式登记，并获发了相应的侨民登记证。

据报道，他抵达哈尔滨时持有相当大的一笔钱，这是他在布拉戈维申斯克的一次起义期间从某些苏联政府机构挪用的。这也据称是他逃离苏俄的主要原因。

1927年，Lovtsoff 前往济南府，加入张宗昌元帅的军队，并在俄国分队中担任牙医直至1928年。

In 1928 he came to Shanghai and for the next two years
did not trouble himself with any work, his means of leaving
being a sum of money that he brought with him.
However, it did not last him long, as he being a very
unbalanced and audacious gambler, lost most of it in various
card games and races.
In 1930 he registered himself as a dental surgeon with the
Health Department of the French Municipal Council and after
approval established a dental office at 318 Rue Cardinal
Mercier.
In 1933 he left for Kuling with a view to establishing his
practice there, but evidently he did not succeed, for in
February 1934 he returned to Shanghai.
After his return he started to practice again at 779
Avenue Joffre, later changing his address to 257 Avenue du
Roi Albert.
V.A. Lovtsoff is not known to have any political affiliations
and while in Shanghai has not come to the notice of the Municipal
Police in connection with any political or criminal activities.

（批：孙）

N. MacPang.
D. S.

1928年他来到上海，在接下来的两年里没有从事任何工作，靠带来的钱维持生活。
然而，这笔钱并没有维持多久，因为他是一个情绪极不稳定且胆大妄为的赌徒，在各种牌局和赛马中输掉了大部分钱财。
1930年，他在法公董局卫生处注册为牙科医师，获批后在梅爱尼神父路318号开设了一家牙科诊所。
1933年，他前往牯岭，打算在那里开业，但显然未能成功，因为他在1934年2月回到了上海。
回来后，他再次在霞飞路779号开业，后来地址改为阿尔贝王路257号。
据查，V.A. Lovtsoff 没有任何政治派系关系，在上海期间也未因任何政治或犯罪活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

Macao, September 22, 1936.

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai.

Sir,

On August 3, a Russian named Venedikzt Alexandrovich
Lovtsoff, 44 years of age, landed here with his wife Ana
Lovtsoff, and two children: a daughter named Zoia Lovtsoff,
14 years of age, and a son named Eugene Lovtsoff, 12 years
of age. Venedizt Lovtsoff first called himself an amateur
musician and afterwards he claimed to be a dentist.

I have the honour to request for information
regarding this man's antecedents including his political
and criminal record, if any. I also take this opportunity
to request that information be sent to us regarding any
suspicious Russians who you may learn are leaving for South
China. Enclosed is a photograph of Venedizt Alexandrovich
and his family.

（批：Noted O.R. 6/10）

(Signed) Alexandre Maher, Captain,
Commissioner of Police, Macao.

D S Makaroff
J.B. 29/9

Macau, 22 de Setembro de 1936

Exmo. Sr.

Tendo desembarcado nesta Colonia, em 3 de Agosto ultimo, com passaporte chinez, o russo Venedikt Alexandrovich Lovtsoff, de 44 anos, casado com Ana Lovtsoff, com dois filhos Zoia Lovtsoff, de 14 anos, sexo feminino, e Eugene Lovtsoff, de 12 anos, sexo masculino, que se apresentou primeiro como amador de musica e por ultimo como dentista, rogo a V. Exa. se digne informar-me do que possa constar a seu respeito, quer politica quer criminalmente, o que antecipadamente agradeço.

Outrosim solicitaria de V. Exa. que, caso fosse possivel, me informasse, na primeira oportunidade, do que constasse acerca de russos suspeitos de que V. Exa. tivesse a indicação de terem vindo para o Sul da China.

Junto um fotografia do russo citado e familia.

Aproveito a oportunidade para apresentar a V. Exa. os protestos da minha mais alta consideração.

A Bem da Nação.

Exmo. Senhor:
Comissario de Policia de Xangai.

O Commissario de Policia e

S. 1, Special Branch /Siddon/. File No.................... Date November 26, 1941.

SUBJECT:
Hung Tsang Cotton Mill - strike.

On November 14, the 2,200 workers employed on
the day and night shifts by the Hung Tsang Cotton Mill,
361 Markham Road, declared a "tai-kung" strike to
enforce demands for improved working conditions.
Work was not resumed until November 22, when some 500
day shift and 400 night shift hands started operations.
The number was gradually increased to 1,500 on
November 25 and the situation is now practically normal.

Immediately before the declaration of the
"tai-kung" strike, the Management issued a notice
announcing an increase of 30% in wages. The workers,
however, were dissatisfied with this grant and refused
to commence work. They were eventually dispersed
from the mill premises by the Municipal Police at
the request of the Management. As a result of the
Police action, the workers alleged that about thirty-
five of their colleagues received injuries.

In the afternoon of the same day, three Chinese
claiming to have been sent by the Western Branch of
the Shanghai Special Municipality Social Movement
Direction Committee, Lane 95, 10 Edinburgh Road, O.O.L.
called at the Hung Tsang Mill with the intention of
conducting negotiations on behalf of workers with the
Management. They were told by the Police of Gordon
Road Station that they were not allowed to function
in the Settlement, whereupon they departed.

恒昌棉纱厂 - 罢工。

11月14日，位于马克姆路361号的恒昌棉纱厂雇佣的2200名日夜班工人宣布举行“怠工”罢工，以强制要求改善工作条件。直到11月22日，约500名日班工人和400名夜班工人开始复工，生产才得以恢复。人数逐渐增加，到11月25日达到1500人，目前局势已基本恢复正常。

在宣布“怠工”罢工前夕，厂方发布通知，宣布加薪30%。然而，工人对这一让步表示不满，拒绝开工。应厂方请求，工部局巡捕最终将工人从厂区驱散。由于警方的行动，工人声称约有35名同事受伤。

同日下午，三名中国人声称受上海市社会运动指导委员会西区办事处（爱丁堡路95弄，O.O.L.）派遣，前往恒昌纱厂，意图代表工人与厂方进行谈判。戈登路分局的巡捕告知他们不得在租界内活动，随后他们离去。

the notice issued by the Management, the wording refers to the "wages", which are more or less beneficial to the employees. The problem was therefore settled without further argument. The management, however, insisted on the dismissal of some 40 workers on suspicion of being agitators. The employers' representatives claimed that this was submitted as a result of a decision reached by the Board of Directors. Despite the fact that the number was reduced to thirteen, the workers strongly objected, resulting in their failure to start work on November 20. Efforts made by the Police succeeded in prevailing upon the workers to partially return to work on November 22.

On the same day, several representatives of the workers also appealed to Mr. P.Y. Koo of the Industrial Section, S.M.C. for assistance. Apart from opposing the dismissal of workers, the labour delegates demanded the payment of wages and allowance for the period of the strike and an additional increase of 30% in the high-cost-of-living allowance.

A meeting was held in the Special Branch Headquarters at 4 p.m., November 24, when both sides concerned attended. Mr. P.Y. Koo of the Industrial Section, D.S.I. Chu Meng Wei of Gordon Road Station and D.S.I. Loh Wei Kong of Special Branch were present. The workers' grievance was conveyed to Mr. Chen Tseng Chong, representing the management. He stated that

同日，几名工人代表也向工部局工业科科长顾振宇（P.Y. Koo）先生求助。除了反对解雇工人外，劳工代表还要求支付罢工期间的工资和津贴，并将生活费用津贴额外增加 30%。

11 月 24 日下午 4 时，在特务总部举行了一次会议，有关双方均出席。工部局工业科的顾振宇（P.Y. Koo）先生、戈登路警署副督察长朱梦伟（Chu Meng Wei）以及特务科副督察长罗维康（Loh Wei Kong）在场。工人的申诉已转达给代表资方的陈增崇（Chen Tseng Chong）先生。他表示

The question over medical expenses incurred by the allegedly injured employees be left for further discussion, and it was also reiterated that the request of employees in the Dyeing Department for the issue of two suits of uniform be referred to the Board of Directors for consideration.
